mean: keeping at something steadily is itself a kind of strength

石の上にも三年 is about enduring a hard situation until it pays off; 継続は力なり is about keeping up a practice, hard or not.

mean: if you really set about it, you can achieve it
lit: do it and it will be done

story.text: The phrase opens a short verse attributed to Uesugi Yōzan, an eighteenth-century lord of the Yonezawa domain, remembered for reforming his debt-ridden domain. Roughly, it says: do it and it can be done; do nothing and nothing will be done; when a thing is not achieved, it is because people did not act.
story.source: Verse attributed to Uesugi Yōzan (上杉鷹山), lord of Yonezawa

use.how: Quoted as encouragement or a motto, often with だ or の精神, sometimes extended to 為せば成る、為さねば成らぬ. Has a rousing, slightly old-fashioned ring.

near.diff: 継続は力なり praises keeping going steadily over time; 為せば成る urges you to commit and act, saying the goal is within reach.
